clue.text: Rider hurt on borders of Cornwall after clipping front of bike

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, its first and its last

parts.note: the first and last letters of Cornwall

indicators.note: clipping a front trims away the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to hurt or mistreat is to abuse
the first letter of bike, which is removed

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist injured near the Cornish border after hitting the front of the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a cyclist, which the surface encourages, but it is a legal term here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause in a legal document or bill, attaching a condition.

clue.text: The end of short troubles, spending a penny

parts.note: curt means brief or short in manner

indicators.note: spending money means it leaves you, and a penny is abbreviated to one letter

parts.note: pains are troubles
P is the abbreviation for penny, removed from the second piece

explanation.surface: Someone briefly troubled, perhaps during a visit to the toilet — 'spend a penny' is British slang for using one.
explanation.walkthrough: CURT plus PAINS with its P removed gives CURTAINS. 'Spend a penny' is British slang for going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Curtains' is informal for the end, especially death or the finish of something, from the theatre curtain falling.

clue.text: Fixed two plugs with worker, having taken day off

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, and day is shortened to its single-letter abbreviation

parts.note: two words for a plug: an AD (a plug is an advertisement) and a DAM (a stopper)
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
D is the abbreviation for day, taken out once

explanation.surface: Someone fitted two electrical plugs with help from a workman who had a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' looks electrical, but one plug is an advertisement and the other a stopper; only one of their two Ds is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means fixed in an opinion, refusing to be moved.

clue.text: Stealthy-sounding tax should be minimal

indicators.note: sounding means we go by how the words are said, not how they are written

parts.note: stealthy means sly
to tax is to test or strain

explanation.surface: A covert levy ought to be kept as small as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'sly test' sounds like SLIGHTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The slightest amount is the smallest possible, so minimal is a synonym.

clue.text: Yours truly, having composed an &lit is giving autographs

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, I

indicators.note: to compose is to put together afresh, so the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the ampersand

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of writing an &lit clue while signing autographs.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit is a clue whose whole text is both definition and wordplay; here it is only fodder. 'Yours truly' ends letters, as initials might.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, someone who initials a document signs it with the first letters of their name, like an autograph.

clue.text: Our car cleaner eating Tesco's top bananas as source of energy

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Tesco, taken in by the other letters

explanation.surface: A car-washer munches on bananas from Tesco, a British supermarket chain, for energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' places T among the other letters, and 'bananas' looks like the fruit being eaten but is the scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates power by fission, making it a source of energy.

clue.text: Thug regularly spent times drinking black stout

indicators.note: every other letter is used up and discarded, leaving the alternate ones

parts.note: first and third letters of Thug

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: times as in multiplication, three by four
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A lout repeatedly drinks dark stout, the Guinness-like beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black stout' looks like the beer, but stout is the definition and black is only the letter that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a person as plump, just as tubby does.

clue.text: 4 of the Commodores rejected plugging when available for shows

indicators.note: something plugging a gap goes inside it

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the letters run the other way in this down entry
4-across is INITIALS, so we want the first letters of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
a new book or record that is out is available

explanation.surface: Initials of the band the Commodores are rejected when fans are available for their shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare number 4 points to 4-across, whose answer tells you to take first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out is to perform or demonstrate, which is what someone who shows a scene does.

clue.text: Prejudice shown by male relative upset about former partner

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns something upside down, so it reads from bottom to top
about means going around, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: short for sister; reversing it changes nothing
an ex is a former partner
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man's sister is upset by bigotry from her ex.
explanation.walkthrough: The short word for sister reads the same both ways, so the reversal changes nothing visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexism is prejudice or discrimination based on a person's sex.

clue.text: Mostly bitter article behind unexpectedly tough finish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: stinging means bitter or sharp, here lacking its final letter
the definite article
a tail is a behind or rear end

explanation.surface: A sour news story about a rear end, ending unexpectedly harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a word of position, but it is a noun for the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting in the tail is an unpleasant surprise at the end of something, like a scorpion's sting.

clue.text: Claret is drunk assuming one's sensible

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the letters take in an extra one
drunk suggests stumbling about, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who has drunk claret claims they are being perfectly reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic person is practical and grounded, which is what sensible describes.

clue.text: In Spar store beside beauty product

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice
to can mean beside or against, as in 'face to face'

explanation.surface: Inside a Spar convenience store, next to a cosmetics shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a chain of convenience shops, but here it is the boxing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Botox is a brand of botulinum toxin injected to smooth wrinkles, sold as a cosmetic treatment.

clue.text: Spiritual leader once more ditching popular mayor

indicators.note: ditching means dumping, so those letters are thrown out

parts.note: again means once more
in means fashionable or popular, removed here
Sadiq Khan, Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Once again a well-liked mayor is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: AGAIN loses IN and gains KHAN, from Sadiq Khan, the Mayor of London since 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aga Khan is the hereditary imam of the Nizari Ismaili Muslims, a religious leader.

clue.text: Altering my tone, getting back to grass roots

indicators.note: altering means changing, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of grass

explanation.surface: Someone changes their voice to get back to grassroots politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass roots' reads as one phrase, but it splits: grass supplies its last letter and roots is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An etymon is the original word from which another derives, its linguistic root.

clue.text: Salt promotion — it requires curbing

indicators.note: curbing means restraining, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: found across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A promotion for salt needs to be restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in promotioN IT REquires.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a salt also called saltpetre.

clue.text: Independent judge locking up Republican prior to appeal causes anger

indicators.note: locking up means imprisoning, so these letters are held within
prior to means before, so one piece comes first

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
to rate is to judge or assess
R is the abbreviation for Republican
it means sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: An impartial judge jails a Republican before he can appeal, which angers people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword convention; the Republican and appeal go together into the judge after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to annoy, so it causes anger in a mild form.

clue.text: Guides briefly woo American city crowd to venture north

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to woo is to tempt, here missing its final T
Los Angeles

indicators.note: going north in a down entry means reading upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a crowd or group of people

explanation.surface: Tour guides quickly persuade a group in Los Angeles to head north.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMP from TEMPT, then LA, then SET read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Templates are patterns used as guides when cutting, writing or making something.

clue.text: Cold month petered out

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
something that petered out eased off

explanation.surface: A chilly month that faded away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold month' reads as December, but Cold is the definition and month alone gives DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead body is cold, so cold is an informal way of saying deceased.

clue.text: Sharply reached a point or was blunt?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: cut (with a blade) to the ..., getting to the point
second meaning: spoke directly, skipping preliminaries

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the opposition of sharp and blunt; the idiom covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to get to the point without wasting time, which is speaking bluntly.

clue.text: Maybe posts online greatly increased?

parts.note: up means increased, as in prices are up
loads means a lot, greatly

explanation.surface: Perhaps social-media posts have soared.
explanation.walkthrough: The two parts come in reverse order to the clue: increased then greatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To upload is to transfer a file to the internet, posting it being one example, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: I'm surprised! The setter reportedly producing nonsense!

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker, shocked, is said to be talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My eye!' is an old exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an exclamation of disbelief meaning that is nonsense.

clue.text: One putting up with cleric online?

parts.note: E for electronic, as in email
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A tolerant person, perhaps a clergyman ministering on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up with' looks like tolerating, but with is just the joining word; online places E before RECTOR, an e-rector.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is someone who erects, or puts up, a structure.

clue.text: Outspoken place of worship starts to overwhelm Welsh city

indicators.note: outspoken means said aloud, so the next word goes by its sound

parts.note: a mosque is a place of worship

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of overwhelm and Welsh

explanation.surface: A loud church overwhelms a Welsh city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh city' wants to be the definition, but Welsh supplies a letter and city alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia.

clue.text: Implied nothing depressing in lecture

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: a lecture is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: bleak means depressing

explanation.surface: Implying nothing gloomy in a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'O bleak' sounds like OBLIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblique remark is indirect, hinted at rather than stated, so it is implied.

clue.text: Rum in France that is seen over here uncased

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: que is French for that

indicators.note: removing the casing strips off the outer letters, keeping the middle

parts.note: the middle letters of here

explanation.surface: Rum that is common in France is found over here without its cask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but it is the old British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British informal for odd or strange, an old sense of queer.

clue.text: Pass on last vestige of knowledge here?

definitions.text: Pass on last vestige of knowledge here?

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: the last remnant of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of knowledge

explanation.surface: A place where teachers hand on the last scraps of what they know.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side and on side are the same half of the field, so on gives LEG. The whole clue also describes a college, where knowledge is passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is an institution of higher education, where learning is passed on to students.

clue.text: See 18
Retiree cycling close to camps holding national traitors

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter round to the back

parts.note: OAP, old-age pensioner, British for a retiree
national as in state-run, a state school

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of camps

explanation.surface: A pensioner cycling near holiday camps detains traitors to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is British for old-age pensioner; its first letter moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, so apostates are traitors to it.

clue.text: Right to stop excess when facing Left's spendthrifts

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so one piece leads the next
a stopper goes into a gap, so this letter is put inside

parts.note: waste is excess or surplus
R is the abbreviation for right
L for left, plus the S

explanation.surface: The political Right's excess against the Left's wastefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: Right goes in before the last letter of the word for excess, and the apostrophe-s of Left's is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastrels are people who squander money, the same as spendthrifts.

clue.text: Woman being free takes time

indicators.note: takes means accepts inside, so these letters admit another

parts.note: as means being, as in 'as a child'
to rid is to free
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman, once freed, takes her time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' as a word for 'as' is an easily missed sense: 'as a child' means 'being a child'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a woman's first name, a Scandinavian one.
